about.text: Pecorino romano is a hard, salty Italian cheese made from sheep milk, often used for grating over pasta or other dishes. The name pecorino means 'ovine' or 'of sheep' in Italian; the name of the cheese, although protected, is a description rather than a brand: [formaggio] pecorino romano means 'sheep's [cheese] of Rome'.

facts.v: Whole fresh sheep's milk; may be thermised
Thin, ivory to straw; may be coated neutral or black
Mostly Sardinia now, about 97% of production; also Lazio and the province of Grosseto
